_: Kill-check for asc-09wx.8.2: the capture, which hashes the files a session is shaped by and records one `intervention` row for whatever moved. Two files carry the claims -- packages/cli/src/watched.ts decides what is watched and what counts as a change, packages/cli/src/commands/capture.ts decides what is written. Every mutant below is a direction one of those can be wrong in, and the dangerous direction is always a FALSE ROW rather than a missed one: a missed change costs one observation and is repaired by the next edit, while a spurious row is permanent (entries are immutable) and is the whole reason `watched-hashes.ts` prefers silence to a claim. Three mutants are of that class -- `vanished-is-not-a-change` under-reports, while `unreadable-reads-as-absent` and `watch-identity-order-sensitive` each produce a row that says a file was deleted or that a whole set was newly created when neither happened. Two more are about the baseline rather than the row (`dry-run-writes-the-baseline`, `applied-not-claimed`) and one is about the watched set itself (`everything-is-a-hook-script`). Killers were found empirically, by planting each mutant and reading the failing test names off vitest's JSON reporter, never by guessing them -- and `unreadable-reads-as-absent` is why that matters. Its first form deleted the `isThere` guard outright, which makes the `return` below it unreachable and costs the `error` narrowing (`error TS18046: 'error' is of type 'unknown'`), so `tsc -b` refused the tree and the runner reported "ran no test" for both killers -- the exact shape a survivor has, from a mutant that never ran at all (`mutation-harness-must-distinguish`). The mutant flips `isThere`'s own return instead -- the same defect stated in the helper rather than at its call site -- and that does compile.
